issues.body:
The sparq-gui crate is excluded from the root workspace, so its only CI coverage is .github/workflows/gui.yml, which builds/clippies/tests exactly four states: default (`cargo clippy --all-targets`, `cargo build`, `cargo test`), `--features federation` (gui.yml:533,536), `--features odrl` (gui.yml:544,547) and `--features custom-protocol` (gui.yml:676,808). `hdt` appears nowhere in gui.yml, and there is no `sparq-gui` entry under .github/feature-matrix.d/ (only crates/sparq-hdt itself is covered there, which does not compile gui/src-tauri/src/engine.rs).

The hdt-gated code in the GUI is real code that has never been type-checked in CI: engine.rs:336-343 (`load_hdt` calling `sparq_hdt::load(path)` and `to_loaded_document`). The only hdt-related test, engine.rs:539 `hdt_import_in_a_lean_build_fails_loudly_with_a_rebuild_hint`, is `#[cfg(not(feature = "hdt"))]` — it validates the lean build and is compiled OUT precisely in the state this PR ships. So the feature state the release now depends on has neither a compile check nor a test.

The workflow is tag-triggered, so this does not run on the PR. On the first `v*` tag a compile error would fail the two Linux rows (soft:false → fails `release`), and on macOS/Windows (soft:true, `continue-on-error` at release.yml:287) an hdt- or platform-specific failure would silently drop those installers from the release rather than surface. That is exactly the class of breakage the repo's "both feature states green" discipline exists to prevent, and this PR makes it load-bearing.
issues.fix_hint:
Add an hdt lane to .github/workflows/gui.yml next to the existing federation/odrl lanes, e.g.:

      - name: Clippy (hdt, -D warnings)
        run: cargo clippy --all-targets --features hdt -- -D warnings

      - name: Test (HDT import, native lane)
        run: cargo test --features hdt

Best is to also compile the EXACT release combination so the shipped state is the tested state, e.g. `cargo clippy --all-targets --features hdt,federation,custom-protocol -- -D warnings` (custom-protocol is what `cargo tauri build` injects). Consider a positive hdt test (import a small fixture .hdt and assert the quad count) so the feature-ON path is not merely compiled but exercised — the current `#[cfg(not(feature = "hdt"))]` test cannot cover it. Land that lane before, or in the same change as, enabling the feature in release.yml.
issues.title: `--features hdt` enables a feature state that is never compiled in any CI lane

issues.body:
gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml documents four opt-in features and states the release intent for each. For `odrl` (sq-ixc3.15) it says verbatim: "The desktop release build turns it ON; the webview/wasm target never links these crates". After this PR the release build does NOT turn it on, so that comment is stale/false — an honesty drift the repo's rules treat as a defect, not a nit. `forms` (sq-1cnox) is worded more loosely ("unless a release explicitly opts into ..."), but the same decision is unmade.

The practical consequence is that shipped bundles keep the loud stub paths: odrl.rs registers a stub that "fails loudly with a rebuild hint" and forms.rs "returns an actionable unavailable error". End users of the released desktop app get an error telling them to rebuild the app themselves for two tools the crate documents as release-enabled.

The selection is also backwards with respect to evidence: `odrl` has full CI coverage (clippy -D warnings + real sparq-policy/sparq-solid tests at gui.yml:544-547), while `hdt` — the feature this PR does enable — has none (see the other finding). The PR enables the untested feature and skips the tested one, with no rationale recorded in the added comment.
issues.fix_hint:
Pick one and make the tree self-consistent:
(a) enable it — `--features hdt,federation,odrl` (and decide explicitly on `forms`), which also matches the existing Cargo.toml comments; or
(b) keep the release set at hdt,federation and update gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml's `odrl` comment (and `forms` if relevant) to state the real, current release posture plus the reason (e.g. "deferred to a later release; tracked in <bead>"), and record that rationale in the release.yml comment too.
Either way the added `[SONNET-4.6] sq-3w29b` comment should say WHY these two and not the other two, so the next reader does not have to diff the manifests to find out.
issues.title: Enabled feature set contradicts the crate's documented release intent (`odrl` claim is now false)

issues.body:
The comment immediately below the changed line (release.yml:430-439) is an explicit honesty ledger enumerating what is proven vs documented-untested for this job, and it was written against the crate's CI-proven default/custom-protocol build. This PR changes the compiled feature set of every row without adding a line to that ledger.

As it stands the ledger reads as though the Linux rows' crate build is fully covered — "Linux rows ...: the GUI crate build + webkit deps are already proven green in gui.yml; the .deb/.AppImage bundle step is the new surface" (release.yml:435-436) — which is no longer accurate: with `--features hdt,federation` the crate build itself is also a new, CI-unproven surface on Linux, not just the bundler. The added comment claims what the change does but is silent about its unproven status, which is the part the ledger exists to record.
issues.fix_hint: Add a bullet to the PROVEN vs DOCUMENTED-UNTESTED list, e.g. "* `--features hdt,federation`: `federation` is proven green in gui.yml; `hdt` and the hdt+federation COMBINATION are compiled here for the first time (no gui.yml lane) — DOCUMENTED-UNTESTED, tracked in <bead>." and correct the Linux bullet so it no longer implies the crate build in this feature state is proven. If the gui.yml hdt lane from the other finding is added, update both statements to match reality instead.
issues.title: The PROVEN vs DOCUMENTED-UNTESTED honesty ledger was not updated for the new feature state

issues.body:
gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml's `custom-protocol` comment records that `cargo tauri build` enables that feature automatically, and that without it the webview navigates to devUrl and shows "Could not connect to localhost" instead of the embedded frontendDist. The release now passes user features on the same command line. tauri-cli v2 documents `-f, --features [<FEATURES>...]` and appends them to the CLI-injected set, so this is expected to be fine — and I could not verify it empirically here (tauri-cli source is not vendored or cached in this checkout).

Worth noting because the failure mode is silent-ish and user-visible: if the injected feature were ever dropped, the bundle would build successfully and only fail at runtime with a connection-refused webview. The flag's position (last on the line, nothing following it) is correct and avoids the multi-value-arg swallowing hazard.
issues.fix_hint: Cheapest coverage is the plain-cargo lane suggested in the hdt finding: `cargo build --features hdt,federation,custom-protocol` in gui.yml compiles the exact shipped feature set without depending on tauri-cli's injection semantics. Alternatively assert on the `--verbose` build log (it prints the cargo invocation) that `custom-protocol` is still present alongside `hdt,federation` on the first real tag run, and record the result in the honesty ledger.
issues.title: Nothing in-repo pins that tauri-cli's `--features` is additive with the injected `custom-protocol`

verdict.summary:
The change adds `--features hdt,federation` to the tag-triggered `cargo tauri build` step so release bundles ship the native HDT importer and the federated SERVICE client. The mechanics are sound: `-f/--features` is a real tauri-cli v2 build flag placed last (so its multi-value parsing cannot swallow another flag), the feature graph resolves (`cargo metadata --features hdt,federation` succeeds in the standalone gui/src-tauri workspace), gui/src-tauri/Cargo.lock already pins sparq-hdt/hdt and ureq/rustls/ring (no --locked in play, and no aws-lc-sys, so no NASM/CMake requirement is introduced on the Windows row), and the security posture of the newly-shipped egress client is genuinely fail-closed (federation.rs installs a strict allowlist-only policy; an empty allowlist refuses every endpoint, pinned by a real test at federation.rs:171).

Two things block approval.

(1) `hdt` is a feature state that is compiled NOWHERE in CI. gui.yml exercises the sparq-gui crate in default, `federation`, `odrl` and `custom-protocol` states only; there is no `sparq-gui` entry in .github/feature-matrix.d/. This PR makes a tag-triggered job — which by the workflow's own admission does not run on PRs — the first place `--features hdt` (and the `hdt,federation` combination) is ever built, on all five OS rows. The macOS/Windows rows are `soft: true` with `continue-on-error`, so an hdt-specific failure there drops those installers from the release without failing it.

(2) The enabled set contradicts the crate's own documented release intent: gui/src-tauri/Cargo.toml says of `odrl` "The desktop release build turns it ON", which this PR makes false. `odrl` has full clippy+test coverage in gui.yml; the PR enables the untested feature and skips the tested one.

No malicious or instruction-like content was found in the diff.
